evidence.observation: Export used by the demo for the create -> activate step. It throws 'WattClaw project and gateway RPC are required' when the project record or RPC function is missing, diffs project.members against agents.list and re-creates only the missing agents through 'wattclaw.team.project.member.update', then throws 'WattClaw agents were not restored: <ids>' if any member agent is still absent after the refresh. It returns { project, agents, restored } where restored is true exactly when the incoming status is 'archived', which is how the demo tells a fresh activation apart from a restore.

Retention sweep that is the only legal producer of a stop. It lists projects via 'wattclaw.team.project.list', filters them with filterWattClawProjectsByOwnedAgents, and archives a project only when it is terminal (success/failed/fail) and its final retention window expired, or when it is 'archived' and its restored access window expired (or it still has loaded agents and was never restored). Everything else is returned in kept/skipped, archive errors go to failed, and the returned object is { scanned, kept, archived, skipped, failed } - the exact contract the demo asserts for legal and illegal stops.

Activation guard rail. It throws 'WattClaw project has no agents' for an agent-less project, returns the agent list immediately when every project agent is already loaded (no gateway reload), and otherwise applies the current gateway config via config.get/config.apply and polls agents.list until all agents exist or it times out with 'WattClaw agents were not loaded: <ids>'. The demo asserts both branches: config.apply is skipped right after member.update restored the agents, and it is used after a simulated gateway restart.

The two stop windows (FINAL_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS = 3 days for terminal projects, RESTORED_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS = 24 hours for restored archived projects) that pruneWattClawProjectsForUser compares against project.updatedAt / access-state restoredAt. The demo mirrors these values and pins them with boundary assertions: pruning 1 ms before a window closes keeps the project, 1 ms after it archives it.

Computes the next retention sweep as 18:00 Asia/Shanghai (UTC+8) on the following day when today's slot has passed. The demo uses the fixed demo clock 2026-08-20T10:00:00.000Z (18:00 Shanghai) and asserts the scheduled stop sweep is 2026-08-21T10:00:00.000Z.

Emits the ownership events for every member of an activated project: trackAgent(userId, agentId, name, { workspace, description }) plus trackSession(userId, `agent:<agentId>:main`, agentId, projectName, 'main'). The demo feeds it the agents returned by activation and records the resulting wattclaw.team.agent.tracked / wattclaw.team.session.tracked events (2 agents, 2 session keys) in the asserted event stream.

Normalizer for nested gateway payloads ({ project | data | result | payload }), used by the demo to normalize the create response before the fixture is driven; it returns the record only when id is a string and members is an array, which is how the demo verifies the created fixture matches the shape the rest of the runtime expects.

The executable demo. It rebuilds a fresh local fixture under .prale-eval/demo-fixture/tenant-demo/.wattclaw-team/projects/p-demo, records every accepted transition in `transitions` (legal flag checked against LEGAL_TRANSITIONS), records every refused attempt in `rejections` together with the proof (error message or prune result) and asserts the event log did not grow, then asserts the exact expected event stream and archive-rpc accounting. Returns the normalized operation result that is written to .prale-eval/demo-run.json.

Frozen table of the only transitions the demo accepts: create absent->created, activate created->active, complete active->terminal, stop terminal->stopped, activate stopped->active (restore), stop active->stopped (restored project after the 24 h window). isLegalTransition() (lines 55-57) is used to fail the run if any observed transition is not in this table.

Resolves a project fixture directory from envConfig.OPENCLAW_CONTAINER_DATA_DIR/<tenant>/.wattclaw-team/projects/<projectId>. The demo uses it to prove the freshly created fixture is written exactly where the runtime looks for project config.json files.

claims.claim: Activation is guarded at both ends: activateWattClawProjectRuntime rejects a missing project/RPC and throws when a project's member agents cannot be restored, so a project can only become active when every member agent is loaded; the demo shows the happy path (2 member.update calls) and the refused-restore failure ('WattClaw agents were not restored: p-demo-degraded-worker') leaving the fixture status at 'creating'.

Stop (archive) is a legal transition only through pruneWattClawProjectsForUser: a terminal project after the 3-day final retention window or a restored archived project after the 24-hour restore window. Illegal stop attempts (in_progress, terminal but 1 ms early, restored but 1 ms early) are returned in `kept` with no archive RPC and no event, and the demo asserts `failed` is empty for both legal stops.

ensureWattClawProjectRuntime refuses an agent-less project ('WattClaw project has no agents') and only performs the config.get/config.apply + polling ladder when agents are missing, so activating an already-loaded project issues only agents.list; the demo asserts both call sequences, including the post-restart path agents.list -> config.get -> config.apply -> agents.list.

The demo fixture is genuinely local and fresh: it is deleted and re-created on every run, persisted as config.json in the layout resolved by resolveWattClawProjectDirectory, and a second consecutive run of the demo exits 0 with identical results (no leftover state is required).

The run observed exactly 6 legal transitions (create absent->created, activate created->active, complete active->terminal, stop terminal->stopped, activate stopped->active, stop active->stopped) and 8 rejected attempts spanning create/activate/stop; every rejection was asserted to add no event and to leave the on-disk fixture status unchanged.

The emitted event stream is deterministic and complete: 15 lifecycle events for the main project (created, 2x member.restored, 2x agent.tracked, 2x session.tracked, updated, activated, updated, terminal, archived, runtime.reloaded, restored, archived) plus the degraded fixture's created event; exactly two archive transitions were applied, both produced by the legal stops, and the rejected bypass attempt was logged but never applied.

conclusion: The demo passes end to end (node server/services/wattclaw-project-runtime.demo.mjs, exit 0, 69 assertions). A fresh local fixture created at .prale-eval/demo-fixture/tenant-demo/.wattclaw-team/projects/p-demo/config.json was driven create -> activate -> complete -> stop -> activate (restore) -> stop, and the WattClaw project runtime accepted only the six transitions in LEGAL_TRANSITIONS: activation is gated by activateWattClawProjectRuntime/ensureWattClawProjectRuntime (project required, agents must be loaded), and stopping is gated by pruneWattClawProjectsForUser's 3-day terminal and 24-hour restored retention windows. All eight illegal attempts (duplicate create, two agent-less/absent activations, an unrestorable member, an in_progress stop both through prune and via a direct archive RPC, and two off-by-1ms window stops) were rejected with no state change and no emitted events, while the emitted event stream matched the expected 16 events exactly and only the two legal stops produced a wattclaw.team.project.archive transition.

validation.notes: Run twice in a row from the repository root: exit 0 both times, fixture deleted and re-created on each run, 6 legal transitions / 8 rejected attempts / 16 events / 69 recorded assertions, and the normalized result written to .prale-eval/demo-run.json. The harness imports the real server/services/wattclaw-project-runtime.js helpers (activateWattClawProjectRuntime, ensureWattClawProjectRuntime, pruneWattClawProjectsForUser, extractWattClawProject, trackWattClawProjectOwnership, nextWattClawRetentionRunAt) and server/services/wattclaw-project-events.js resolveWattClawProjectDirectory, so failures fail the run with a non-zero exit code. LIMITATION: node_modules is absent in this checkout, so the repository's vitest suite (npx vitest run server/services/wattclaw-project-runtime.test.js) could not be executed; the dependency-free demo harness covers the same module surface (activation, retention/archive legality, ownership tracking, retention schedule) and was used instead.
